maybeUseful.title: How we cut Next.js memory from ~5GB to ~1GB
maybeUseful.description: React-query v3 starts a timer for every query during server-side rendering. Node ties each request's context to that timer, keeping the entire request in memory until the timer fires, up to 5 minutes later. Setting cacheTime to Infinity on the server prevents the timer from starting, since the query client is thrown away after each render anyway. Memory dropped from 4.8 GiB to 1.2 GiB per pod after the fix.
maybeUseful.reason: This article explains a specific memory leak in React-query v3 during server-side rendering, where Node.js timers keep request contexts in memory. It provides a concrete configuration fix that significantly reduces memory usage for Next.js applications.

summary:
This week, we processed a significant volume of technical updates focusing on the architectural shift toward persistent AI agents and the rigorous engineering required to secure and scale modern software systems. 

**The rise of persistent agentic systems** is driving a new set of architectural requirements for engineering teams. For those building autonomous workflows, [Building always-on agents](https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-always-on-agents?utm_source=tldrai) provides a foundational look at persistent memory and core loops, while [Shopify's Agentic Vulnerability Hunting System](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fshopify.engineering%2Fcyber-chaos-monkey%3Futm_source=tldrinfosec/1/010001a1e4b20e87-6e0849bc-0b29-405f-8b00-8b9bdf5ba137-000000/rJqaTK6ZsvozOpGeDsf89Qy3GwLK2ypJq1WJWpRvLVg=452) demonstrates how these patterns can be applied to production security. To ensure reliability, teams should look into [degrading gracefully](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fincident.io%2Fblog%2Fdegrade-gracefully-designing-ai-features-that-keep-working-when-the-model-doesnt%3Futm_source=tldrdevops/1/010001a1e444a765-4f73171b-062d-435f-9ffa-56eb5ea36da3-000000/tqcdSS8ZHGh68XWW3M9ewvE7imFDtjyIIGGWljLswVU=452) when models fail and adopting [eval-driven development](https://www.langchain.com/blog/what-is-eval-driven-development?utm_source=tldrdev) to move past "vibe-based" testing. It’s also worth considering how [AI speeds up coding but can slow down delivery](https://programmingdigest.net/links/23702/bbbff61a-89f9-4346-842d-648091b4f029/email) by creating review bottlenecks, reinforcing the argument that [the answer to AI is more rigorous engineering](https://ghuntley.com/answer/?utm_source=tldrnewsletter).

**Hardening the modern stack** requires both cutting-edge verification and a return to first principles. We’re seeing a paradigm shift in security through [formal verification of Signal’s codebase](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.r2tkAX6RdgQsMKMmEZrF6GRZlJ8AAQ9IGoz2q83cMItQW_8X3nsx3vnRFA00ER0Nt804sA_OO_9_pn_UKTv5rNdwz6fZvGozf0T6BFXvJmE7vcCP5pKgz_hSFFBrshZB0ZvtHBxroJQJepBv27ThDw/4vo/tfBbZyFjTZaNU73YbXX1-A/h44/h001.7WOMQCunWiACi1p2XaktL7fV3_wi5pJLyV_JqVye5bc) and new research on [securing AI supply chains](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.ph_QWNSUqNc4t8_ksAzZPnDt476Y6EI8WJtAPc5IWgK3GC_XmWMyWg92uU_wYUixP6RiV4FLw2jhb2bFtf1HStf-i-972Gioslsa3RlsgPgqRZX3nP41ZQWmp7wHLW4xUgL7qZYyx_s8JOr3GSFucbG97qE40dsHsOQN4WJ5eZi8KUyEtkgMbcCtl5x4T_8Be6bdvWJIDxk0z0MW239kx6hco5ngWXpw3ojyRqXgkn8/4vo/tfBbZyFjTZaNU73YbXX1-A/h119/h001.uUbfa9sg8Yk3NhOzzyCok0xI8BXjX8zJ9IGqlsoDt3o). On the infrastructure side, there are practical lessons to be learned from [post-quantum authentication migration](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.ietf.org%2Fblog%2Fiab-pq-workshop-impressions%2F%3Futm_source=tldrinfosec/1/010001a1e4b20e87-6e0849bc-0b29-405f-8b00-8b9bdf5ba137-000000/Y9iomUMFCE9Bzey7u6Z3TAG_OE5IvEw_6YCFDgtkKPM=452) and [speeding up CI](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.freecodecamp.org%2Fnews%2Fspeed-up-ci-in-the-age-of-ai-written-code%2F%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a1e44ad1f3-87bfb640-95de-4ced-82f6-b8a5af10ed5d-000000/Dx3pPUxEJAdP37tkHQyiJYL5rT7ESAQoWlMlHFHOPwQ=452) in the age of AI. For frontend developers, a specific [Next.js memory leak fix](https://reactdigest.net/links/23709/005da204-b193-4903-93ee-bbd0f8df73fd/email) involving React-query timers is essential reading. Finally, we should periodically re-evaluate our technical intuition, whether that’s avoiding the [‘Is-A’ trap in inheritance](https://programmingdigest.net/links/23706/bbbff61a-89f9-4346-842d-648091b4f029/email) or reconsidering [previously dismissed "bad" ideas](https://devonestes.com/bad-ideas-that-arent-bad-anymore?utm_source=tldrnewsletter).

**Optimizing the development environment** involves a mix of self-hosted utilities and specialized AI tooling. For local testing, the [AWS Emulator](https://github.com/aws/aws-emulator?utm_source=tldrdev) and [Uptime Kuma](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Flouislam%2Fuptime-kuma%3Futm_source=tldrdevops/1/010001a1e444a765-4f73171b-062d-435f-9ffa-56eb5ea36da3-000000/QjCUofQtQ-mBeO2LnvaCDFXU5C-VVXWAarU03AYQUMw=452) offer great alternatives to cloud-heavy workflows, while [Protomaps](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fbruceroettgers.eu%2Fblog%2Fprotomaps%2F%3Futm_source=tldrdev/1/010001a1e44ad1f3-87bfb640-95de-4ced-82f6-b8a5af10ed5d-000000/KVqA2lWa9cU0F93DmyeuG8bofoPftsNasrapYVzsdj0=452) makes self-hosting map tiles surprisingly accessible. Mobile engineers might find value in [analyzing cold start performance with Perfetto](https://us.list-manage.com/B2UWEmz2mU0?e=e6b8ce3dfb&c2id=46e5652986e7ba42471a8d4daf1044f2) or exploring [Kotlin Multiplatform iOS build bottlenecks](https://us.list-manage.com/1AFw5TYYSd9?e=e6b8ce3dfb&c2id=46e5652986e7ba42471a8d4daf1044f2). There are also interesting niche tools like [installctl](https://github.com/yamixst/installctl?utm_source=tldrinfosec) for auditing installers and [Signet](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FWhispergate%2FSignet%3Futm_source=tldrinfosec/1/010001a1d018c3f2-e248130c-c72f-45f1-9810-029441c48ff0-000000/ocG1BO6yNag8qyOAEci19qm9hY6MYkl5AcBfm_9yoC4=452) for automated code signing.

**Deep-tech explorations in AI** are uncovering both performance gains and new attack vectors. Research into [end-to-end 4-bit training](https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/end-to-end-4-bit-training/?utm_source=tldrai) and [integer-only arithmetic for deterministic inference](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fnathan.rs%2Fposts%2Fdetllm%2F%3Futm_source=tldrai/1/010001a1d54e9017-686d3c18-da41-4905-9057-8739ae4d5bdb-000000/eCmtKF28ZZzde67T45YM3UOIZJrrq7UhayLo4nlkhhk=452) target the efficiency of local models. However, these advancements come with risks, such as [AI agents being backdoored by editing fewer than 10 neurons](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fthehackernews.com%2F2026%2F11%2Fmicrosoft-researchers-show-ai-agents.html%3Futm_source=tldrinfosec/1/010001a1d018c3f2-e248130c-c72f-45f1-9810-029441c48ff0-000000/pLmpDwADRxBlaIfUYWVyzputGRfiWO70a5hpoqeBszA=452) or [prompt injection risks in npm releases](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fthedefiant.io%2Ffrontier%2Fai%2Fresearchers-say-codex-flaw-put-npm-releases-at-risk%3Futm_source=tldrinfosec/1/010001a1d018c3f2-e248130c-c72f-45f1-9810-029441c48ff0-000000/tE3hR4qjshYnMg80D8s3mo1FEMdg5lXQmqBjIRI45D0=452). To stay ahead, teams can look at [ARTEX for AI-powered red teaming](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Funit42.paloaltonetworks.com%2Fartex-and-ai-powered-red-teaming-tools%2F%3Futm_source=tldrinfosec/1/010001a1d53f3d4a-73118516-e7da-472d-8ecb-3787244a3b68-000000/OX_rwAlr0S-4nNVipYFNJiKIi2iMG5suoqeBexAX4mA=452) or [Wazuh](https://tracking.tldrnewsletter.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fwazuh%2Fwazuh%3Futm_source=tldrinfosec/1/010001a1d53f3d4a-73118516-e7da-472d-8ecb-3787244a3b68-000000/051OTuHHoaqA7zEpIdAnJ3yHhDXrfhz-jlhhqPUfWBQ=452) for broader threat detection.
